question: In the Li3PO4-coated NCM study, how much did the charge-transfer resistance rise over 50 cycles for the bare and the coated material, and what capacity did each retain after 100 cycles at 1C?

rendered: Charge-transfer resistance (Rct) from the EIS spectra measured during cycling in the Li3PO4 (LPO)-coated NCM study. Bare NCM: Rct increased from 27.99 to 224.04 Ω[1], a rise of 196.05[2] ohm. LPO-coated NCM: Rct from 14.88 to 144.75 Ω[3], a rise of 129.87[4] ohm, so the coating roughly halved the rise. Capacity retention when cycled at 1C between 2.8-4.5 V[5]: bare NCM retaining 75.4% of its initial discharge capacity after 100 cycles[6]. LPO-coated NCM has a capacity retention of 88.4%[7]. The document reports these retentions as percentages of initial discharge capacity, not as absolute mAh/g capacities.
